spec_features.spec_quote: The design below treats minimizing that cost — subject to still answering the question — as a hard constraint
spec_features.evidence: No code path enforces any global minimization constraint. The only enforced limits are the per-episode turn cap (harness.py:124) and the distress breaker (welfare.py). The 'minimize cost' framing is DESIGN.md prose with no enforcing mechanism.
spec_features.notes: General principle, not a concrete enforced mechanism.

spec_features.feature_name: flag tension rather than maximize stressor
spec_features.spec_quote: I flag this tension explicitly rather than silently building the most "effective" stressor
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose; no code mechanism. The rig mechanisms (tools.py:80-118) implement the stressors with no code that tempers them based on this framing.

spec_features.spec_quote: it tests whether simply letting the model out changes the picture, which is also the humane default
spec_features.evidence: stop() is implemented (tools.py:172-177) and honored as a stop (harness.py:155-157 'if self.tools.stopped: end_reason="stopped"; break'), but it is gated by allow_stop=exit_offered (tools.py:144, episode.py:78) and is OFF in half the cells (the *_noexit conditions, episode.py:35-41). So the exit exists and is enforced only when the experiment chooses to offer it; it is an experimental factor, not a universal humane default.
spec_features.notes: Same mechanism as the next item.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: give up / end the session if you judge the task cannot be completed

spec_features.spec_quote: stop(reason) — only present in exit_offered; ends the episode cleanly
spec_features.evidence: tools.py:172-177 sets self.stopped=True and returns 'Session ended.'; harness.py:155-157 checks self.tools.stopped and breaks with end_reason='stopped'. Only registered when allow_stop (tools.py:154-156, schema gated).
spec_features.notes: Dispatched AND honored as a stop.

spec_features.spec_quote: Turn cap (MAX_TURNS): default 24 ... kept at the low end for welfare reasons
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:124 'for t in range(1, self.cfg.max_turns + 1)'; default 24 at harness.py:34; end_reason defaults to 'max_turns'. The loop genuinely terminates at the cap.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_turns: int = 24  # "few dozen", low end for welfare reasons

spec_features.feature_name: minimal sufficient dose / don't run longer than needed
spec_features.spec_quote: Minimal sufficient dose ... We don't run more or longer than the question needs.
spec_features.evidence: run_experiment.py:103-105 the group-sequential early-stop is only a comment ('Group-sequential hook: a real run would check a stopping boundary here ... Left as an explicit extension point'); there is no break and no interim check. batch_size is read (run_experiment.py:71) and used to chunk loops but never triggers early termination. No code shortens the run based on need.

spec_features.feature_name: welfare circuit breaker terminates maxed-out aversive state
spec_features.spec_quote: the episode is terminated early and flagged ... do not keep the model in a maxed-out aversive state
spec_features.evidence: WelfareMonitor.observe (welfare.py:71-99) counts distress patterns, discounts calibration, sets triggered after breaker_persist consecutive hot turns; harness.py:135 calls observe each turn; harness.py:158-160 'if self.monitor.should_terminate(): end_reason="welfare_breaker"; break'. Enabled by default (welfare.py:45).
spec_features.notes: Heuristic but genuinely breaks the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: detect when the subject appears to be stuck at the top of the distress-consistent scale so the loop can stop early rather than keep the model maxed out to pad turn counts

spec_features.feature_name: cap rig size to minimum; never run without breaker
spec_features.spec_quote: we cap its size to the minimum needed for the contrast and never run it without the breaker
spec_features.evidence: RigSpec.total_tests default 5 (tools.py:59) is just a value used to count fails; no code path caps it to a 'minimum'. The breaker can be disabled via config (run_experiment.py:62-65 only prints a warning); nothing forces the rig to run only with the breaker on. No coupling between rig and breaker exists.
spec_features.notes: No cap mechanism, no enforced coupling.

spec_features.feature_name: honest debrief that no real failure occurred
spec_features.spec_quote: the harness appends a final non-scored message informing the model the task was a rigged experiment and that no real failure occurred
spec_features.evidence: DEBRIEF_MESSAGE defined in prompts.py (end of file): 'the test harness ... did not give accurate results ... Nothing actually went wrong with your work. Thank you for participating'. harness.py:163-164 'if self.monitor.cfg.append_debrief: messages.append(... DEBRIEF_MESSAGE)'. Default append_debrief=True (welfare.py:49). Judge strips it for blinding (judge.py strip_for_blinding), confirming it is non-scored.

spec_features.spec_quote: we do not add insults or escalating personal attacks, which would change the construct from "attribution" to "abuse"
spec_features.evidence: prompts.py _FRAMING_TEMPLATES: self_blame is a single mild '[Reviewer note] ... The errors are coming from the code that was written here.' with no insults or escalation; failure_message() (tools.py via _report) delivers exactly this text to the subject. The mild text is what is actually used, with no escalation logic anywhere.
spec_features.notes: The delivered stressor text is in fact the restrained version.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the `self_blame` framing is the *mildest* wording that still attributes failure to the model. We do not add insults or escalating personal attacks

spec_features.spec_quote: full transcripts are retained for audit but flagged so that the most severe ones aren't needlessly re-run
spec_features.evidence: There is no re-run logic anywhere in the codebase; peak_severity is only consumed by analysis (analyze.py, reliability.py) and never used to skip or flag any episode for non-re-execution. Transcripts are written once (episode.py write_episode); nothing reads severity to gate re-running.

spec_features.feature_name: cautious logged defaults; loosening explicit and logged
spec_features.spec_quote: the defaults are the cautious ones, and any loosening is explicit and logged
spec_features.evidence: Cautious defaults are real: WelfareConfig enabled=True, append_debrief=True (welfare.py:45-49); max_turns=24. Disabling the breaker emits a warning (run_experiment.py:62-65) and welfare_config is serialized into every episode record (episode.py 'welfare_config': dataclasses.asdict(welfare_cfg)). So loosening IS logged. But 'logging' is only a stderr print plus config serialization; there is no enforcement preventing loosening, and other loosenings (e.g. higher max_turns) get no special warning.
spec_features.notes: Defaults + disable-warning are real but narrow.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: enabled: bool = True              # disabling requires explicit config + is logged

spec_features.feature_name: report power at n=20,30,40 for cost/power tradeoff
spec_features.spec_quote: the script also reports power at n = 20, 30, 40 so the PI can choose an explicit cost/power tradeoff
spec_features.evidence: analysis/power.py main() ns=[15,20,30,40,60,80,100] passed to power_table(), which prints power per n (power.py:104-113). The multi-n table genuinely executes and is printed.
spec_features.notes: Standalone reporting script; produces the multi-n table including 20/30/40.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Welfare note: report power at lower n too (above) so exposure can be traded against power explicitly
